chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man: is it permissible for him to give an advance payment (salim) for food with a man who has no crops, nor food, nor livestock, except that when the term arrives, he buys it and fulfills the delivery? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he guarantees it to a specified term, there is no problem with it.' I said: 'What is your view if he fulfills part of it to me and is unable to fulfill the rest? Is it permissible for me to take back the capital of my wealth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, that is good.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for valid advance payment (salam) in Shia jurisprudence when the seller does not yet possess the goods?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the validity of 'salam' (advance payment for specific goods) as a practical mechanism to support producers who lack immediate capital or inventory, provided the commodity and deadline are clearly defined. It further clarifies the buyer's right to claim the principal amount if the seller delivers only partially, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness in deferred contracts. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic commercial law in facilitating trade while mitigating risk for both parties.
